item.title: Rockstar Games crammed a lot of content into GTA 6, but fan-favorite mini-games like darts and bowling didn't make the cut because the team didn't have "unlimited money or unlimited time" to do those activities justice.
item.description:
Rockstar Games crammed a lot of content into GTA 6, but fan-favorite mini-games like darts and bowling didn't make the cut because the team didn't have "unlimited money or unlimited time" to do those activities justice.
Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson explained why the studio chose to focus on some aspects of development and not others during an interview with VGC. As noted by the site, picking up a game of darts has proven to be a good pastime in games like GTA 5 and GTA Online, but in GTA 6, the standards were a bit higher.
From NPCs to the feel of motorized scooters, Leonida is Rockstar's most realistic playground yet. Every blade of grass was given special attention, and while pool was one game the team was able to fully realize, not everything panned out like they had hoped. Nelson said "darts was a contentious one" when talking about the decision to cut it from the game, explaining that it was left behind because the team didn't have the resources to do it right.
GTA 6 Side Activities
"Even we… you hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to," he said.
Nelson elaborated, saying that, starting with Red Dead Redemption 2, the team started to treat mini-games more like activities. In other words, bonuses like darts became less about being a diversion of Rockstar's open worlds and more of an extension of them. The goal is to make pool, darts, or any other activity feel like it's just as punchy and weighty for Jason and Lucia as it is in the real world.
Using GTA 6's in-game workouts as an example, he added, "You’re not just pushing a button; it mimics what weightlifting is."
"A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right," Nelson continued. "Darts is one we just didn’t get to."
Long story short, Rockstar just "didn't have the resources" to make it "feel proper." His thoughts on the matter – or any scenario where a mechanic or activity is cut – were summed up in one line: "It’s better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough."
GTA 6 is now the highest-rated game of all time. IGN gave it a 10/10 review.
For one of the better examples of the care the developers put into side activities, look no further than some of the games Jason has on his JoySystem. You can see how Rockstar pulled from real-world inspirations to create his character here.

item.title: Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life.
item.description:
Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life.
As 13 years of waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto ended last week, players have found themselves enamored with Jason Duval. Stoic, nonchalant, calm, composed, resigned; whatever you want to call one of GTA 6's new protagonists, Rockstar says it carefully crafted his already iconic demeanor by pulling from a Steve McQueen classic and real-life veterans.
The studio's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, talked about how the studio behind the mega-hit video game built Jason from the ground up during a conversation with Destructoid. Centering the story on a "couple on the run" marked new territory for Rockstar, but it's far from a new concept in entertainment. So, the team turned to movies, particularly Sam Peckinpah's The Getaway.
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
"Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone," Humphries explained. "We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite."
He continued, saying that Rockstar's research into real-world veterans and Army Rangers helped refine its approach. Those who have played the game (and keen-eyed trailer watchers) already know about Jason's military background, so the influence here definitely tracks.
"These guys typically aren’t running their mouths or reacting to something unless it’s strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves."
Jason is the talk of Vice City and has been for some time. As Rockstar shared more details about its seemingly shy lead ahead of GTA 6's launch, some fans began to wonder if he could be the franchise's first-ever neurodivergent protagonist. In addition to his personality, Humphries described Jason as "wired differently" during a recent interview with Love magazine.
While Jason steals more than just wads of cash in Vice City, his partner in crime has proven to be just as impactful. Game writer Michael Wiafe said looking into the kind of criminal activity known to make headlines in Florida was one of the first things the team did when creating both Jason and Lucia. For Rockstar, it wasn't just about creating true-to-life criminals; it was about creating fully realized human beings.
"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn’t stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What’s important is how they resonate, no matter where you’re experiencing the game in the world."
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
Between the chaos of robbing gas stations and drug dealers and getting into high-speed car chases, Jason and Lucia can become quite the power couple. Game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern said to Destructoid, "You really want them to make it." The quiet moments where the duo scrolls through social media in their bed or drives the other one to work can be just as important as the action set pieces. Gauvey-Kern added, "Those need to hit too, and you need to connect with how the characters are feeling in those moments."
Although GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S three days ago, Leonida is packed with enough things to do to keep players playing for months. While we wait to see what's next for Rockstar, you can check out IGN's 10/10 review. You can also read about how the developers made every NPC feel like real people you could run into on the street.

item.title: Director Luca Guadagnino has confirmed his American Psycho remake is officially dead.
item.description:
Director Luca Guadagnino has confirmed his American Psycho remake is officially dead.
The Challengers and Call Me by Your Name movie maker delivered the disappointing news when asked for an update on Deadline's Crew Call podcast. He admitted the script for the project that he read, which was penned by the writer behind The Bourne Ultimatum and Side Effects, was "fantastic" but not something he can continue working on.
"American Psycho, which is a fantastic script from Scott Z. Burns, unfortunately, is not happening for me, as we speak," Guadagnino said.
The Folio Society's American Psycho Illustrated Edition Image Gallery
Guadagnino has more than proven himself as a name capable of handling the weight of a property on the level of American Psycho, which is exactly why movie fans were so excited to hear he could be attached to the project in 2024. Although fans have referred to what would have become his slice into the well-established movie universe as a 'remake,' at the time of its announcement, Lionsgate teased that the project would have been more of an adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' American Psycho novel, rather than a remake of Christian Bale's 2000 movie.
Updates on Guadagnino's American Psycho have been few and far between in the years since its announcement, though. Elvis star Austin Butler was once in the running for the role of Patrick Bateman, as was Euphoria's Jacob Elordi. It was reported in October 2025 that the film would not gender-swap its lead role.
Bale eventually went on to comment on Guadagnino's reimagining and another actor bringing his iconic character to the big screen. He said "all the best to 'em" just earlier this year, adding, "I like brave people."
The director didn't explain why his version of American Psycho won't be moving forward, just that it's "not happening for me." While that means any version of American Psycho won't be coming to movies anytime soon, it's unclear if Lionsgate has completely closed the door on Patrick Bateman. With Burns' script finished, there's always the chance a different filmmaker could take the reins.
For now, though, it's best to assume the American Psycho remake/adaptation is well and truly dead. In the meantime, Guadagnino is gearing up for the release of his Sam Altman biopic, Artificial. The film is gearing up for a limited premiere Christmas 2026 before getting a wider release January 8, 2027.

item.title: The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen.
item.description:
The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen.
McMillen and Nicalis spent months building up to the November 19, 2026, release date for the latest update in their classic action roguelike game, but that launch was quickly soured. Just 8% of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent Steam reviews are positive, with a good chunk of comments left by players referencing AI-generated material that was not previously mentioned in any official capacity.
"Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one popular review said.
Screens - The Binding of Isaac Repentance
"I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds to refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," another said. "Shameful they would do this to an Indie gem. Shameful."
The allegedly AI-generated content in question seems to be music exclusively tied to a specific, Grand Theft Auto-themed run meant to coincide with the recent release of GTA 6. What could have been a cute jab at another gaming titan boiled into a full-blown controversy for Nicalis when Reddit user ShweetsStuff reported the questionable tunes just one day after launch.
As artificial intelligence advances, it's become increasingly difficult to discern human-made art from content pushed out by machines, but ShweetsStuff was able to provide evidence backing their claims. Specifically, they pointed to a handful of tracks that mention AI music software Suno in their metadata, which also included links to their Suno pages.
AI-generated content passed off as art has already become controversial on its own in recent years. Adding to the fire for The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was the fact that the music was featured in the new update without any sort of update to its Steam description. Valve requires developers to disclose how they may have used AI during game development, making the music's inclusion as puzzling as it is concerning for those who felt Nicalis had pulled the wool over their eyes.
Negative reviews poured in following ShweetsStuff's discovery, leading McMillen to issue a statement today. He said he “had no idea" how AI-generated music found its way into the launch build of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s new update.
"Woke up to a s**t show," he said, "obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned."
Please report issues and bugs to the email attached.
Just hours later, Nicalis launched a new patch, confirming the "removal of generated music files." The update is currently live for PC, with the studio adding that it has already been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony. When exactly it will go live for those platforms remains to be seen.
No explanation for how or why the AI-generated music was included was provided. Instead, the team simply said it was "working on the game and will continue to address new and old bugs." McMillen also encouraged fans to report issues and bugs to the developers.
In the meantime, The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent reviews on Steam remain firmly in the "Overwhelmingly Negative" category. The major update also coincided with the launch of Repentance+ on new platforms, including Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. For more, you can read IGN's 9/10 review for The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth and our 9/10 review for Afterbirth+.

item.title: GTA 6 players on PlayStation 5 have reported frequent crashes tied to error code CE-108255-1, and it looks like it's blocking them from progressing through the story while they wait for Sony and Rockstar to send out a fix.
item.description:
GTA 6 players on PlayStation 5 have reported frequent crashes tied to error code CE-108255-1, and it looks like it's blocking them from progressing through the story while they wait for Sony and Rockstar to send out a fix.
Although Rockstar Games spent a decade making its new Grand Theft Auto game, it's no surprise to see the new highest-rated game of all time launching with at least a few hiccups. Some have it worse than others, though, with more than a few reports of crashes affecting PS5 consoles popping up online in the days following GTA 6's launch.
The most common cause seems to be tied to error code CE-108255-1, which, as defined by Sony, simply indicates that "an error occurred with the game/application." It seems that, although the majority of players aren't encountering the issue, those who have haven't been able to find a proper fix. Adding to the trouble is that those who have met these dreaded GTA 6 crashes are getting them pretty frequently, and what's triggering them isn't always clear. There are reports from players on both standard PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles running into these issues, with some even saying that crashes appear to be tied to the story, barring them from making any progress.
"I've noticed that the issue manifests differently for different players," one Reddit user said. "In my case, the game crashes on Jason's loading screen: it freezes and then displays the CE-108255-1 error code, meaning I can't even get into the game. Others manage to play for a few minutes before experiencing a crash. I really hope Sony and Rockstar work together to investigate and resolve this issue as soon as possible."
Game crashes are annoying for anyone, but when a massive game like GTA 6, which many feel has a less-than-generous autosave system, suddenly boots players back to the PS5 home screen without warning, it can be especially troublesome. Many who have reported the crashes to PlayStation Support say they've been directed to Rockstar, while those who report to Rockstar say they're being directed to PlayStation. One player said they feel like they're "stuck in an endless support loop, with a game I paid for and still can't play."
Meanwhile, those who have managed to get help say most assistance hasn't been able to completely resolve their issues. However, some have said they've had luck with a few tried-and-true methods, such as uninstalling and reinstalling the game, making sure both the PS5 and game have their most recent updates, and restoring licenses.
"I’ve done everything possible to solve this," another player said. "Deleted cache. Rebuilt database, deleted everything else from my console, took it apart, cleaned it, turned HDR off, switched to 1080p, went and updated game license, deleted and reinstalled and still crashing. Ugh. I’ve got a day 1 PS5 with a disc drive. Other friends of mine with the same console are playing with no issue."
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
Again, it's unclear if the crashing issue is tied specifically to the PS5 or GTA 6 itself. Until either entity comes up with an update, though, all affected players are stuck on launch weekend.
GTA 6 released for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19 and, in its first 24 hours, made Rockstar $3.79 billion. It's the most successful launch in the history of entertainment, and although its exact unit sales have yet to be disclosed, parent company Take-Two Interactive was at least willing to share that it sold 32.5 million copies in pre-orders alone.
For more, you can read about the players unhappy with how Rockstar handled Jason's secret stash. You can also see the lengths the developers went to in order to create realistic NPCs, as well as the Neuralink user who spent launch driving around Leonida with his mind.

item.title: Avengers: Doomsday star and Captain Carter actor Hayley Atwell appears to have let it slip that a new Avengers: Doomsday trailer is set to premiere Monday.
item.description:
Avengers: Doomsday star and Captain Carter actor Hayley Atwell appears to have let it slip that a new Avengers: Doomsday trailer is set to premiere this Monday.
The longtime Marvel Cinematic Universe actor volunteered the information to a group of fans following a performance of her new Broadway play with Tom Hiddleston, Much Ado About Nothing (via @HayleyAtwell_CN on X/Twitter). When one fan shared their hopes to see the short-lived Agent Carter show return, Atwell admitted that "we'll need to see what happens" with Doomsday first.
"There's a new trailer, I think, dropping on Monday," she said with some hesitation. "Am I allowed to have said that?"
Hot Toys Avengers: Doomsday - Lord Doom Figure Image Gallery
Uncertain or not, MCU enjoyers have been on the edge of their seats waiting for what is expected to be the final trailer as Marvel enters the home stretch to the film's premiere. A few short teasers here and there have helped with the wait, but really, the last full-length trailer actually arrived all the way back in August.
As Doctor Doom's assault on the multiverse looms, we're overdue for another look. That said, it has become increasingly clear that Marvel wants to keep most of the movie's big reveals for those who actually make the trip to theaters to see it. While another trailer likely may not be worthy of a slew of new YouTube reaction videos, it's still sure to have a few goodies to entice viewers to make the trip.
Atwell said that, as far as she knows, the new Doomsday trailer will premiere at some point Monday, November 23, 2026. If, for some reason, Marvel decided to push this alleged trailer back, she was able to report that whatever she saw was "amazing."
Hayley, "There's a new trailer I think, dropping on Monday. I watched the trailer. I was like, this is amazing."Fan: "I heard very sad though. We're going to all cry."Hayley, "There's going to be some feelings."Via. cginolfi23🗓20th November 2026 stage door.#HayleyAtwell https://t.co/6TxzspanAT
"I watched the trailer. I was like, 'This is amazing,' she continued. When one fan asked if Doomsday will make everyone cry, Atwell shrugged, mouthed the word 'maybe,' and said, "There's going to be some feelings."
Avengers: Doomsday kicks off the beginning of the end for this chapter of the MCU when it premieres December 18, 2026. A collection of new posters was revealed earlier this week. Next year, the MCU will end the multiverse saga with Avengers: Secret Wars, a movie that MCU boss Kevin Feige has teased will be unlike anything movie watchers have ever seen.

item.title: A Neuralink participant has shared a video showcasing how the technology has allowed him to drive boats, fly planes, and get in shootouts in GTA 6 with his mind.
item.description:
A Neuralink participant has shared a video showcasing how the technology has allowed him to drive boats, fly planes, and get in shootouts in GTA 6 with his mind.
Neuralink shared a video of one of its few participants playing Rockstar Games' latest on social media yesterday. The two-minute highlight reel showed how the individual can use the brain implant tech to take Jason through Leonida with ease, saying that previous methods would often leave him sore.
Playing GTA VI with a Neuralink https://t.co/ViFjXK9OSV
"Before the old chip and surgery, I was using a mouth stick and an iPad," he explained. "I was essentially like a bird, just pecking at an iPad. There was a few games I could play, but obviously, it made your jaw sore and everything sore.
"So then, I get a chip, and it's like, 'What does this let me do?' Immediately, controlling a computer is like, 'boom.' Portal to the world. You just immediately get your portal to the world back."
Rockstar spent 13 years painstakingly crafting the world of GTA 6 to ensure every blade of grass and every line of dialogue was given an unprecedented amount of detail. Although it's maybe truer to life than some may have hoped, there's no denying that the amount of freedom the studio gives players to do everything from robbing banks to diving for sunken treasure has attracted tens of millions of players.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
Despite guiding Jason and Lucia through GTA 6 by different means, the Neuralink participant shown today is one of those millions. In a follow-up post, the tech company, which was co-founded by controversial figure and billionaire Elon Musk, reiterated that the participant and others like him are part of an extremely limited clinical trial.
"Neuralink devices are investigational and have not been approved by the FDA or other regulatory authorities," it said. "This content features voluntary clinical trial participants sharing their personal experiences, which may not reflect all participants or future outcomes."
The first human patient to enter the Neuralink program used it to stay up all night playing Civilization 6 in 2024. A few months later, he was playing Slay the Spire.

item.title: Director Bassam Tariq has opened up about why he exited Marvel's Blade movie, saying, "life's too short to make s**t films."
item.description:
Director Bassam Tariq has opened up about why he exited Marvel's Blade movie, saying, "life's too short to make s**t films."
The Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother filmmaker explained his reasoning for walking away from the Mahershala Ali superhero period piece during an interview with The New Arab. With just one other feature film (Mogul Mowgli) under his belt at the time, working on Blade presented quite the opportunity, but his short time attached as the flick's first director wound up being more of a learning lesson than anything else.
"It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script," Tariq said when asked what working in the studio system taught him. "You're sitting there and explaining to actors what their role will be, and they just have to believe you.
Ranking Phase Five of the MCU
"That's also very dangerous because if the text comes and it doesn't add up to what you were saying, your credibility gets completely shot. All I have is my integrity, and I've been thinking about that a lot."
Marvel Studios announced an Ali-led Blade film in 2019 and picked Tariq to lead the charge in 2021. A little more than one year later, and the director was said to have bounced off the project, with Marvel telling The Hollywood Reporter that "shifts in our production schedule" were to blame.
Today, one new director and multiple frustrated Ali updates later, and Blade has been finally, officially canceled. Marvel Cinematic Universe orchestrator Kevin Feige said the process made him feel like a "gigantic loser and failure" – an assessment Ali agreed with – but for Tariq, the decision to cut off his relationship with Blade came down to how it was impacting his relationship with the film's actors. He told The New Arab that being "the bearer of bad news to your actors" while a corporate entity makes all of the major decisions in the background is "not a great way to be a director."
Avengers: Doomsday Poster Montage Gallery
"I know some people can take that and run with it, but I learned I was losing credibility with my actors, and it wasn't a healthy way to operate as a filmmaker. Life's too short to make s**t films, so that was my big lesson: I have to have full control over my script. If we disagree, it's between them and me. It's quite sad because we had such high hopes for what we wanted to build."
For now, as Marvel heads into another major release with next month's Avengers: Doomsday, there seems to be no sign of a live-action Blade for the MCU. Although the process of trying to get the movie out the door seems to have been tumultuous behind the scenes, there doesn't seem to be any bad blood from Tariq. In fact, when talking about how exiting the film made him feel like a failure last month, the director defended Feige, calling him a "good dude."

item.title: Rockstar made NPCs feel alive in GTA 6 by "establishing deep backstories for almost everything" throughout Leonida.
item.description:
Game developers often refer to their open world cities as characters due to the sheer craftsmanship involved in building out a believable, diverse playspace for the player with its own districts, history, and architecture. This is truer for GTA 6 than most games, but what makes Leonida really feel alive — outside of the puddles of bin juice, the regional-specific cop cars, and mapped out power grid — are the people who live there.
GTA 6 feels like a massive evolution in what it means to be a non-player character (NPC) because there’s an emphasis on the “C” — they’re actually characters in their own right. NPCs don’t just all look unique — with body types, skin, dress style, and hair making them stand apart — they have their own personalities and temperaments. Start a fight with one NPC and they might fight back, while another runs away. One could start a fight by slapping you, another might flick their cigarette at you or tip their drink over your head. Passersby can cheer the fight on, flee, or get involved. Some stop after a single punch knocks sense into them, while others swing until they’re out cold.
No matter where you go in GTA 6, it feels like a lived-in world, on the macro and micro scale. There are over 100 interiors to explore, and each house tells you a story about its occupants. Listen to conversations out on the streets and you’ll get a window into their minds, built out by an entire Rockstar studio dedicated to making them authentic and believable, while still being larger-than-life, funny, and often unhinged.
GTA 6 Bikini Girl Screenshots
“A big part of it was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories,” said Steven Messinger, Rockstar's senior design director for the open world. “For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we’ve fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they’re distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer.
“Players will only pick up on bits and pieces of this, but having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren’t there.”
To build this tangible sense of place, Rockstar takes in-depth research trips for GTA games, embedding the writers in the mundane and the more extreme to really capture the soul of a city. Helicopter trips of the Florida Keys, ride-alongs with police, talking to people, taking photos and notes, all build up a snapshot that Rockstar bottles up to digitize in video game format.
“We had a lot of fun trying to capture the raw energy and vibrant chaos that Florida is known for,” said senior design director of world and population, John Macpherson. “By immersing ourselves into a number of these locations on reference trips, spending time with locals, experiencing as much as possible firsthand, we gathered a direct sense of what would make Leonida feel truly alive.
“Everywhere you look, little stories constantly unfold. It could be as simple as what someone’s wearing, how fit they are, how they walk and talk, who they’re with, what tunes they’re blasting as they cruise down the street. We tried to match that in-game as much as possible, hopefully resulting in something that feels full of life.”
You can walk along Vice Beach and see sugar daddies with their trophy wives, locals playing volleyball, tourists sunbathing, and people walking their pets. Everywhere you look, there’s something happening in Leonida, and it’s completely enveloping. You feel like a part of its world, rather than a godlike being with total control over it.
There’s a mission around the midpoint of the game where protagonists Jason and Lucia people-watch from a hotel sunbed, inventing backstories for the guests by the pool, and it’s something I found myself doing as I explored the world and passed people by, such is the variety and diversity of the game’s NPCs. No other game has ever had such a colorful cast of extras, which is wild when you consider all this was built to add credibility to a world you can zoom past at 100mph.
“We evolved from monolithic NPCs built to visual standards that were lower than the main cast in GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, to fully fleshed-out characters with singular awareness and visual identities,” said Valmor Garcia, senior technical art director on GTA 6. “They are driven by dynamic moods, personalities, unique anatomy, facial features, and dialogue that are visually on par with our protagonists, Jason and Lucia.”
Rockstar built entirely new technology for GTA 6 to simulate hair, cloth, and the way muscles move under the skin. All that work is implemented equally across all characters, so there’s never that uncanny moment where you come face-to-face with a flat and lifeless NPC, staring at you with dead eyes. Everyone you meet is equally detailed, and the range of visual design is staggering.
Of course, this approach created challenges in other areas of development. It’s fairly straightforward to implement a combat system in a game where all character models are approximately the same size, but the varied body types of GTA 6 meant Rockstar had to take a look at how it approached animations so physical contact looks good no matter how big or small the character models are. Especially since this is a game where the two leads can also change in size through diet and exercise.
“We decided early on that we wanted to really push the variation in character sizes and body types,” vice president of animation, Mark Tennant, explained. “This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat.
“Developing this workflow meant that we needed our animators to adopt new techniques compared to a more traditional approach. We also had to grow a team dedicated to overseeing the implementation, which required close collaboration with the art and rigging teams. All these aspects needed to come together to make it work, so it was a huge team effort.”
It wasn’t just player-on-NPC contact that needed to be considered either. There are dozens and dozens of scripted scenes dotted about Leonida to find, the usual Strangers and Freaks of Rockstar games weaved into the fabric of the world, manifesting as wacky encounters of various size and scope. Some are one-on-one, but sometimes you become a spectator as two NPCs with opposing goals clash. If you decide to intervene, the game has to account for every possible permutation of that.
“Shifting the centre of action off the player at times required a lot of careful thought too — if a cop is doing a stop-and-search on another criminal in the world, how do they behave if you commit a crime in front of them?” vice president of design Stephen Donkin explained. “Do they switch their attention to you? Do they compare the severity of the crime? If they come after you, what does the original criminal do? Does he drive off? What happens if you follow him?
“Every event, encounter, interaction had to be considered with this level of depth, as there are so many possible inputs to any given situation, and every new feature or mechanic that is added becomes a new input we must collectively consider.”
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
It’s astounding that Rockstar managed to keep this level of detail consistent over a full playthrough. Even 140 hours in, I’m still seeing new things and being blown away by the level of reactivity in every facet of the world, from Jason’s “mmm, chicken” when he kissed Lucia while she was tucking into off-brand KFC, to the police calling off a stop and search because I pulled my in-game phone out to record them.
GTA 6 is a towering achievement made by a development team of perfectionists, and we likely won’t see anything quite like it until Rockstar does it again.

item.title: Lexie Shoaibi, the actor who plays Mandy in GTA 6, is speaking out now that the game has been officially released worldwide.
item.description:
Lexie Shoaibi, the actor who plays Mandy in GTA 6, is speaking out now that the game has been officially released worldwide.
GTA 6 is finally here, and players have wasted no time looking up the actors behind some of its colorful cast of characters. As the days go on, more and more performers are revealing that they played a part in the game — and one of these is going particularly viral due to a mystery surrounding their character.
The actor who plays Mandy, a character players encounter early in the game, identified herself as Lexie Shoaibi, an American model and actress based out of New York. She posted the news on her Instagram account on November 19, where she revealed that she provided both Mandy’s voice and motion capture.
“She’s a lot of fun, so if you play the game, let me know if you find me,” she said. In another post, Shoabi thanked Rockstar for casting her in the game, writing, “Y’all there aren’t words!!!! Thank you so much for the love and support. This is crazy!! Ily forever!”
Warning: Spoilers for GTA 6 ahead. Turn back now if you want to remain unspoiled!
Mandy is a character who’s been put under the microscope due to a few odd details that players noticed in her home. If you’ve played the first few hours of the game, you’ll know that Jason gets called over to collect rent from Mandy, who says she won’t pay up until her sink is unclogged. Jason finds the source of the clog — all while fending off aggressive romantic advances from Mandy — which appears to be a human fingerbone. Mandy snatches it from Jason’s hand and runs off with it before he can get a good look at what it really is.
A quick stroll through her home and backyard show even more disturbing bits, such as a body-sized hole in the back garden and tubs of acid. The trunk of her car has also been packed with tools that could feasibly be used to kidnap or kill a victim. With all this in mind, fans are convinced that Mandy is actually a serial killer who seduces her victims. (Jason’s loyalty to Lucia really paid off!)
Commenters were quick to praise Shoabi for her performance as Mandy and joke about her uncomfortable, one-sided crush on Jason, with one joking, “Why’d you do that to a committed man?”
“BRO. You had me in a chokehold, but I have to stay loyal to Lucia. Sorry Mandy!!” another said.
“Mandy listen… Look, I know we got off on the wrong foot, ok? Give me another chance,” another wrote.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
If the serial killer theory is true, it means she might not be the only murderer around; fans also spotted references to Dexter in the game, prompting even more curiosity as to Mandy’s true intentions.

item.title: Comcast has said GTA 6's launch triggered the busiest traffic day the company has seen since it was founded in 1963.
item.description:
Comcast has said GTA 6's launch triggered the busiest traffic day the company has seen since it was founded in 1963.
The latest record broken by Rockstar Games' latest actually comes from one of the biggest media and technology companies in the United States. After previously reporting that Grand Theft Auto had led to a 4x increase in traffic on Xbox consoles November 18, Comcast has now confirmed that pre-loads for the day resulted in the busiest day it has ever seen – and it wasn't close.
Comcast recorded peak traffic 31% higher than the average day and 9.6% higher than the previous record holder. Moreover, GTA 6 has resulted in five out of 10 of the busiest days the network has ever seen. Even more remarkable is the news that, as reported by Comcast, 24% of all of its internet traffic during peak times was from users downloading and playing the game.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
If Rockstar fans weren't playing GTA 6, they were watching it. Twitch traffic increased by almost 50% on November 18 and is continuing to rise in the days following that launch. GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, but thanks to the New Zealand trick, a massive chunk of players actually took their trip to Leonida hours early. It certainly helped boost traffic across the board, and in Comcast's case, it resulted in its busiest day ever.
To put some of these numbers into perspective, the company shared a very relevant measurement. November 18 traffic generated on PlayStation and Xbox alone delivered enough data for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K… for two days straight.
It's shocking to see how GTA 6 affected Comcast, but then again, we've known Rockstar's new game would be a juggernaut when it eventually launched. The developer's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, reported that it had earned an unbelievable $3.79 billion in the first day after its release. That makes it not just the biggest video game launch of all time, but the biggest entertainment launch across any medium.
GTA 6 Side Activities
Critics everywhere helped GTA 6 earn the title of highest-rated game of all time. IGN was included in that list after delivering a 10/10 review. We said, "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

item.title: Walker Scobell and Aryan Simhadri revealed that they would watch Attack on Titan fan edits to help them prepare to film emotional scenes for Percy Jackson and the Olympians.
item.description:
Walker Scobell and Aryan Simhadri revealed that they would watch Attack on Titan fan edits to help them prepare to film emotional scenes for Percy Jackson and the Olympians.
Attack on Titan is one of the most popular anime series in the world, in no small part due to its tragic storylines and brutal, gory battles. It’s been more than a decade since the anime first released in 2013, and fans have been making AMVs of their favorite characters ever since — but these fans probably didn’t know that their creations would help high-profile actors tap into their emotions.
Speaking at 92NY on a live episode of Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast, Walker Scobell revealed his unique method for getting himself into an emotional state in preparation for sad scenes while filming Percy Jackson and the Olympians.
Percy Jackson Season 1: Episodes 1-8 Gallery
Scobell said that he would watch fan-made edits for Eren and Mikasa, two of Attack on Titan’s main characters, set to the opening song of Season 3, Red Swan.
“I was trying to get sad. I was in school, and I snuck my phone in. I was like, ‘What can I do to make myself cry?’ I searched up a bunch of — and he did the exact same thing, and we just figured this out yesterday,” Scobell said, pointing to co-star Aryan Simhadri.
“We didn’t communicate this at all. We just ended up doing it,” Simhardi confirmed.
“I thought of the saddest thing I could, and I searched up Eren and Mikasa edits from Attack on Titan,” Scobell continued. “I started crying at school, watching them to Red Swan. And then I got there [on set], and I couldn’t do it.”
Walker & Aryan saying they watch eren & mikasa edits so they can cry on set is actually frying meee 😭😭😭 https://t.co/7JgZFv91Dr
Fans in the crowd had excited reactions to this revelation, as did fans online when clips from the episode made their way on social media shortly thereafter.
“Their tragedy is so profounddd everyone can feel it… oh they really are modern day Romeo and Juliet,” one fan wrote on X/Twitter.
“Red Swan is a Top 3 OP, I don’t blame him,” another said.
“The way they're emotionally regulating through anime edits on a professional set is the most Gen Z actor thing I've ever heard,” another remarked.
It’s no wonder that actors take notes from Attack on Titan for their own projects; in fact, Eren’s English voice actor, Bryce Papenbrook, revealed that he literally unhinged his jaw while screaming in one of the anime’s most iconic scenes in an effort to really sell the character’s pain and confusion.
Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3, The Titan’s Curse, is streaming on Disney+ and Hulu right now with new episodes dropping every Friday through December 11, 2026.

item.title: GTA 6 players are being locked out of in-game stores because they don't own the Ultimate Edition, and they've got some thoughts about how Rockstar handled it.
item.description:
GTA 6 players are being locked out of in-game stores because they don't own the Ultimate Edition, and they've got some thoughts about how Rockstar handled it.
We've known for months that the developer's latest sprawling open-world video game would have a $79.99 Standard Edition and $99.99 Ultimate Edition to pick up at launch. Those willing to pay the $20 upcharge netted a solid assortment of cosmetics, weapons, vehicles, and unique shops, leaving those who didn't shell out the extra cash with fewer options to choose from when taking Jason and Lucia out into Vice City.
Rockstar has been clear about what this would mean for standard owners, but in practice, players are feeling like the door has been (literally) closed in their faces. GTA 6's exclusive in-game shops – One-Eyed Willie's, Sara's Unisex Salon, Stock 305, and Electric Fang Tattoo Parlor – are the topic of conversation here. Not everyone was sure how exactly these stores would bar players from entry upon release. It seems, at least based on the consensus from disappointed players, they were expecting to at least be able to enter the locations and not buy anything – but Rockstar doesn't even give them that.
GTA 6's Ultimate Edition grants you access to a few stores across Leonida, so what happens when you try to enter them in the Standard Edition? #gta6 https://t.co/GMaHpdLwnc
We broke down the Standard vs. Ultimate Edition contents with a side-by-side video that you can check out above. As you can see, the shops have fully decorated interiors that are completely closed off to those who didn't pick up the more expensive version of GTA 6. Those who spent the extra dough can go about their days shopping as they please, while those who didn't have found an unwelcome surprise when heading to any of these spots in Leonida.
Being physically locked out of the building is maybe a bit more brutal than some were expecting, but it's the reality players are meeting – and they aren't happy. Comments from disgruntled fans online have called Rockstar's move to keep content blocked off "greedy" and "shady," with many upset that a relatively substantial amount of finished content is only accessible by spending more money. Others are disappointed to see that there wasn't a cheaper compromise, such as making exclusive shops a late-game unlock. Either way, it's the door in the face that seems to sting the most.
"I'm all for companies making money - but when you pull the kinda money rockstar is - this just feels greedy/shady," one player said.
@IGN https://t.co/BWg2G4TQHk
"Paid $80 just to get bounced from a store like I'm under 21," another replied.
"So the Ultimate Edition just locks the door in your face?" another player reacted. "That's the most expensive closed sign I've ever seen."
GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19. Whether you decided to pick up those extra cosmetic options or not, Rockstar seems to be quite pleased with the release. Earlier today, it noted that it had secured the biggest entertainment launch in history with $3.79 billion in just 24 hours. IGN gave the game a 10/10 review.

item.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly threatened employees with violence and "humiliated" them for decades.
item.description:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly threatened employees with violence and "humiliated" them for decades.
According to sources speaking to The New York Times, Huang — who stepped down as Nvidia's CEO amid a scandal involving infidelity and alleged espionage — has a history of using threatening language against employees.
Several alleged quotes from Huang are cited in the report, including an incident where Huang reportedly told an employee he wanted to rip their head off and "pee on [their] brain."
Nvidia GeForce RTX 30-Series Reveal
In another incident, he is quoted as saying, "You have to do this, or I will rip your f***ing heart out and stomp on it." Others described an incident in which he allegedly went around a room and said he would kill managers, and allegedly said that everyone hoped an employee in their 70s would die soon.
He is also alleged to have told a member of staff: "I’d rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you." It is further claimed that he described receiving verbal humiliation like this as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia.
This language was described as "foundational" to Huang's style of leadership, and is said to date back to the 2000s. The New York Times said some employees who complained about Huang's behaviour received settlements, and that HR was aware of his alleged behaviour.
One settlement was made with the former senior vice president of HR, Michael Winston, it was claimed. Winston was said to have described Huang's behaviour as "verbally abusive, threatening and intimidating." It is reported that his settlement totaled more than $1 million.
Huang denied Winston’s allegations in a statement issued to The New York Times. Nvidia declined to comment.
Earlier this week, Huang said he was ready to return to the company he co-founded, while apologizing for the problems he'd caused both Nvidia and his family. In a statement, Huang insisted he would be willing to return as CEO if Nvidia's Board of Directors decided it was in the best interest in the company.
Some Nvidia employees and other tech CEOs have rallied to Huang's defense and called for him to be reinstated as CEO. The New York Times report alluded to this, acknowledging that Huang does have a following within Nvidia. The attitudes towards Huang are described as "cultish" in the report, with the former CEO alternating between praise and ridicule. It is alleged that he "ruled through fear."
Huang is reportedly due to appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select Committees on December 1. "The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal,” Reps. Brian Mast, R-Fla., John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and Rick Crawford, R-Ark., the chairs of the Foreign Affairs, China Select and Intelligence Committees, said in a statement reported by CNBC.
Photo by Nadja Wohlleben/Getty Images.

item.title: Kaiji Tang, the English voice actor behind iconic anime characters like Jujutsu Kaisen’s Satoru Gojo and Demon Slayer’s Sanemi Shinazugawa, was left stunned after learning that he had unknowingly recorded lines for GTA 6.
item.description:
Kaiji Tang, the English voice actor behind iconic anime characters like Jujutsu Kaisen’s Satoru Gojo and Demon Slayer’s Sanemi Shinazugawa, was left stunned after learning that he had unknowingly recorded lines for GTA 6.
It seems like some of GTA 6’s cast are just now learning that they were featured in the game, as evidenced by a few posts circling online a day after its official global release. One of these cast members is prominent voice actor Kaiji Tang, known for providing the English voice for several main characters in popular series like The Apothecary Diaries, Kengan Ashura, and Baki, just to name a few.
In the early morning hours of November 19, Tang posted on X/Twitter confirming he was in Rockstar’s highly anticipated crime-sim. However, he revealed that he wasn’t aware the lines he recorded were going to be used in this particular game, leading to a hilarious interaction with a fan.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
“I had no idea what I recorded was for this game,” he wrote. “Imagine my shock.”
“Considering they had you saying, ‘Sit on daddy’s lap,’ I’m curious what you thought it was for,” a fan replied.
“I dunno, Demon Slayer?” Tang answered.
i had no idea what i recorded was for this gameimagine my shock lol
@actualcannibal i dunno demon slayer?
Tang is a major figure in the voice acting business with an extensive portfolio under his belt, so it’s no surprise to learn that he lent his talents to GTA 6. Aleks Le, another popular voice actor in anime and video games, revealed that he also contributed to the project, and even said that he asked the directors for permission to include one of his famous lines from Street Fighter 6 — though it’s still unclear if that particular phrase made it into the final product.
Tang isn’t the only actor just now learning they’re in GTA 6; athlete, author, and influencer ‘Jessishiking’ revealed that they were also just now made aware of their involvement in the game.
In a celebratory post on Facebook, Jess revealed that they played the GTA series’ first-ever nonbinary character (which, to avoid spoilers, we won’t name here). They said that they were required to sign several NDAs and had no idea what they were filming for at the time due to the extreme secrecy around the game.
“Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago,” they wrote in their post. “Some fun facts: GTA was one of the most inclusive and caring sets I’ve ever been on. I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly. At the time I wasn’t allowed to know what I was shooting — I didn’t get confirmation until TODAY that it was, indeed, GTA 6.”
While the game’s full credits have since been revealed, it’s highly possible that we see more posts like this in the coming days from voice actors and performers excitedly learning that the secret project they recorded lines for many years ago is the biggest entertainment product of all time.

item.title: Rapper Sexyy Red has given a hilarious response to her cameo in GTA 6 after a clip of famous streamer IShowSpeed playing the game went viral.
item.description:
Rapper Sexyy Red has given a hilarious response to her cameo in GTA 6 after a clip of famous streamer IShowSpeed playing the game went viral.
Warning: Spoilers for GTA 6 ahead! Turn back now if you want to remain unspoiled!
Sexyy Red is one of several real-life music artists who have cameos in GTA 6. Players come across her on a mission playing as Jason, who escorts the rapper into the VYB nightclub in Vice City after getting hired as a security guard. Eventually, Jason gets wrangled into dancing with her onstage, but he quickly backs out after getting a text from Lucia, who is also on a job at the club.
IShowSpeed, one of the internet’s most popular personalities, played through this part of the game during a livestream on YouTube and was stunned after Lucia texted Jason asking, “What are you doing?” Needless to say, Speed was shocked by how quickly Lucia was seemingly able to figure out what Jason was up to.
The moment went viral on social media and was even spotted by the rapper herself, who replied with a hilarious tweet: “We was just chillin’ mane.”
We was just chillin mane
Jason and Lucia’s romantic relationship is a central part of GTA 6, so it’s no surprise that Jason was a bit antsy about dancing with another gal. In fact, it’s one of the main reasons why players can’t hire prostitutes in this game.
Rockstar explained this change in a statement earlier this month, saying, “GTA 6 is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run. While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in 6 has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell… Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTA 6, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia's story.”
Aside from her cameo in GTA 6, Sexyy Red is an avid gamer; in October, she called out NetEase over Storm’s Legendary skins (or lack thereof) in Marvel Rivals, asking the developer in a pointed tweet, “When y’all gon give Storm her legendary skin?”
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
As previously mentioned, Sexyy Red is just one of several actual artists in GTA 6. Pinkpantheress hosts her own radio show in the game, as does Lana Del Ray, Bad Bunny, Freddie Gibbs, and even Kodak Black. The official soundtrack also features a slew of licensed and original songs from high-profile artists like Cardi B, Tame Impala, and many more.

item.title: Macaulay Culkin has reportedly signed on to return as Kevin McCallister in a new Home Alone sequel for Disney.
item.description:
Macaulay Culkin has reportedly signed on to return as Kevin McCallister in a new Home Alone sequel for Disney.
Details on the original child actor's return to the franchise were originally reported by Puck. The project, which would see Culkin slip back into the mind of one of the most mischievous characters in movie history, is said to be in early development at Disney – and it's already got other interesting names attached, too.
Included in the lineup of talent in the mix are The Studio and This Is the End collaborators Evan Goldberg and Seth Rogen. The comedy duo have signed on via their Point Grey banner to produce the Home Alone follow-up and will also help Culkin hammer out the details of the movie's plot.
There have been a number of Home Alone sequels since Culkin helped launch the classic Christmas franchise in the '90s, but most would agree that it's been hard to top the story of the McCallister family. Only the original film and its Lost in New York sequel managed to capture the kind of holiday magic that has brought viewers back in droves through the decades, and that's largely thanks to Culkin's performance.
The now-grown actor has remained the literal poster child for Home Alone for all this time, and in 2026, he's not just ready to come back as Kevin; he apparently pitched the idea himself. Deadline corroborated Puck's reporting and explained the extent of Culkin's involvement in its own piece. The star is said to have pitched his idea for a Home Alone return to Disney Motion Pictures boss David Greenbaum over the summer. One early idea Culkin had involved bringing Kevin back on the big screen as an older, wiser version of the character who also happens to be a dad now.
Whether Kevin would be forgetting his own children at home or dealing with burglars himself yet again remains to be seen, and it's unclear if anything from Culkin's early pitch will make it into the final picture. It's been 34 years since the star last (officially) played the abandoned McCallister boy, so should the early-in-development movie eventually come to be, it will bring an end to decades of fans asking for him to return.
Home Alone House Airbnb Images
Culkin's return as Kevin would mark his third time playing the character and the seventh entry in the franchise. The last, a Disney+ exclusive called Home Sweet Home Alone, premiered in 2021 and starred Archie Yates, Ellie Kemper, and Rob Delaney. IGN gave it a 6/10 review, saying that it "contains wit and heart, if not also clumsy messaging and some tonal misfiring."
For more, you can see Culkin defend his stance that Die Hard is not a Christmas movie. You can also read about how original director Chris Columbus is apparently not a fan of those sequels.
Photo by Kayla Oaddams/WireImage.

item.title: Rockstar Games has confirmed GTA 6 retail sales reached $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours, securing its place as the biggest entertainment launch of all time.
item.description:
Rockstar Games has confirmed GTA 6 retail sales reached $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours, securing its place as the biggest entertainment launch of all time.
Parent company Take-Two Interactive announced the news today. Rockstar founder and president Sam Houser shared his feelings about the landmark achievement in a statement.
"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," he said. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you."
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
After quickly emerging as the highest-rated video game of all time, breaking records across streaming sites, and causing wild spikes in internet traffic, we all kind of knew this was coming. After 13 years, Rockstar has pulled off the greatest score anyone has ever seen. Even in this new update, Take-Two said it was "proud" to help GTA 6 adopt its new crown.
Earning $3.79 billion in 24 hours is unheard of across any medium, meaning Rockstar's new Grand Theft Auto game didn't just stomp on launch sales for games like Red Dead Redemption 2, Cyberpunk 2077, or any Call of Duty game; it crushed any blockbuster movie release ever, too. It's still got a ways to go before claiming any titles like 'best all-time sales,' but it's a start better than anyone has ever seen in the history of gaming.
Just yesterday, it was reported that GTA 6 had managed to sell more than 20 million pre-order copies. Courtesy of Take-Two today, we now know that, somehow, these already staggering numbers actually significantly undershot the reality. The company has now confirmed that it actually moved 32.5 million pre-sale units alone. That's more copies than the vast majority of games have ever sold. Meanwhile, how many non-pre-ordered copies have been sold after launch is unclear.
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19. If this news is anything to go by, Rockstar is just getting started. IGN gave the game a 10/10.
For more, you can see why some players are clamoring for the developers to come up with a fix for Jason's clunky stash mechanics. You can also read about how some people are already asking Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick for an update on GTA 7.

If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks, or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips. item.title: The next Baldur's Gate 3 prequel novel has been revealed, focusing on Shadowheart.
item.description:
Shadowheart is the next Baldur's Gate 3 character to get a prequel novel after "Astarion" by T. Kingfisher released earlier this year.
Published by Penguin Random House, Baldur's Gate 3: Shadowheart, written by Tasha Suri, is already available for preorder at major retailers like Amazon. It will launch next year on June 8, 2027.
Here's the official blurb:
"A calculating priestess must investigate a brutal murder in this darkly fantasy from the World Fantasy Award winning author of the Burning Kingdoms trilogy.
Shar's blessings upon you.
Her name is Shadowheart. As a devotee of the dark goddess Shar, she knows little more about herself than this. But she does know faith and power, and what it takes to keep them.
In the end, all else is detail.
Beneath the bustling city of Baldur’s Gate and within the secretive, underground church she calls home, one’s past is a weakness best sacrificed to the fathomless Mirror of Loss. With oblivion comes strength, but without the bonds of memory, treachery festers among even the most ardent of Shar’s acolytes.
"When a member of their order is killed in the Upper City, Shadowheart and her so-called allies are called to investigate. She trusts none of them: not Mirie, the ambitious Griefguard; not Caldan, the cynical propagandist; and certainly not Nocturne, the charming quartermistress, who claims to have only Shadowheart’s best interests in mind.
But the wealthiest district of Baldur’s Gate has secrets of its own, and it hides temptations far greater than any Shadowheart remembers facing. Torn between the familiar comforts of the dark and the thrill of new desire, she must solve the mystery to prove her devotion… or be cast into the light."
Some fans r/BaldursGate3 had might already noticed there was a Shadowheart book in the works after several international Amazon stores posted a description for the now confirmed book.
But, excitement may be tepid from fans, since feedback for T. Kingfisher's Astarion prequel have been mixed. Fans have called out several retcons to the vampire's backstory, while also lamenting that the book "doesn't do justice to his character".
While Larian has left Baldur's Gate 3 and the Dungeons & Dragons universe behind to work on brand new games, including Divinity, it lives on. HBO is working on a Baldur’s Gate 3 TV show set after the video game, which not all fans are thrilled about.
Many can’t fathom why anyone would want to continue on from the events of Baldur’s Gate 3, given its many different endings, variances in world state, and, most importantly, the vastly different outcomes for beloved characters such as Astarion, Karlach, and Shadowheart.
Hasbro also plans for a video game follow-up to Baldur’s Gate 3, but whether that’s a Baldur’s Gate 4 that continues the story or something entirely different remains to be seen. In the meantime, these books will give fans something to chew on.
Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.
You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.
His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides.
